outcome: Major: false scale-dependent bilinear estimate on core proof chain

source_location.proof: Appendix pp.656-658 / PDF pp.24-26, particularly (59) and next sentence
source_location.application: Equation (37), p.648 / PDF p.16; Proposition 3.3 p.649; Theorem 1.2 proof p.655

confirmed_findings.source_claim: Uniform L2 bound for integral Q_t rho dot Q_t F^t m(t) dt/t by C ||rho||BMO ||N(Q_t F^t)||2 for arbitrary bounded compact F(x,t).

counterexample.F: F_N=1_Q cos(q_j x1) on I_j and 0 elsewhere
hypotheses_verified: rho and F real and measurable; both bounded by1
rho spatially compact and BMO norm<=2
F supported in Q x [5^-N,2/5], compact subset of R2 x (0,infinity) for every finiteN
Exact vector kernel t grad P_t used; the uncut comparison has only its first derivative component
Non-tangential maximal norm uniformly bounded by local bound1 and |x-(pi,pi)|^-4 tail
counterexample.calculation: Exact torus moments E g^2=N/2 and E g^4=3N^2/4-3N/8 imply E|g|>=sqrt(N/6). Uncut bilinear average equals A E|g| with A=(3e^-2-5e^-4)/4. Cutting both inputs changes normalized E-average by at most 3/(64pi^2). Thus L2 output >=2pi(A sqrt(N/6)-3/(64pi^2)), while claimed RHS remains uniformly bounded.
counterexample.proof_of_failure_for_all_constants: Let N tend to infinity; no universal C can satisfy the claimed bound.

confirmed_findings.suspect_step: General reduction from nonzero output-frequency support to arbitrary equal kernels; lowpass multiplier in square function after (59) cannot be bounded uniformly because it tends to identity as t->0.
counterevidence_considered: Uniform L-infinity bound instead of BMO also fails for this family.
Spatial compactness of both inputs is already imposed.
Every finite member has t-support bounded away from0; smooth approximations can preserve the obstruction.
Application kernel t grad P_(t/2) has the same obstruction, with positive scale factor 2/e-3/e^2.
The original separated-function Coifman-Meyer setup is not being refuted.
Family is not a coupled convection solution; main physical theorem is not disproved by it.
confirmed_findings.core_dependency: Proposition2.3 -> equation37 / Proposition3.2 -> Proposition3.3 -> Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.3. Later boundary correction does not provide replacement.
confirmed_findings.repair_boundary: No verified replacement sufficient for temperature slices. Restricting F to fixed-underlying-function form removes the example's freedom but is not justified for arbitrary height-dependent temperature slices; new PDE structure or another analytic estimate is needed.

unresolved_claims: Whether the final physical heat-flux theorem can be established by a valid alternative argument; no physical PDE counterexample is claimed.
historical_note: Authors' arXiv record states early withdrawal over scaling and former Proposition3.1; not relabeled as this current finding or claimed independently reproduced.

independent_acceptance_check.scope: Focused acceptance of existing F01, including uniform quantifiers, complete vector kernel, localization error and core dependency.

checks.result: Every finite-N input has compact support in the open upper half-space, bounded real values, BMO<=2 and a uniformly bounded non-tangential maximal L2 norm. Exact lacunary moments yield sqrt(N/6), the paired term has positive A=(3e^-2-5e^-4)/4, and the cut-off error is bounded by3/(64pi^2). Thus no universal constant satisfies Prop2.3.

The t grad P_(t/2) variant has positive factor2/e-3/e^2. Source (37)/Prop3.2 to Prop3.3 to Thm1.2 gives a core derivation dependency. This does not construct a violating coupled PDE solution or certify a complete repair. The low-pass square-function step is part of the same problem.

independent_acceptance_check.result: Existing F01 remains Major; no scientific change required.
